purpose: Haloperidol is used to treat conditions like schizophrenia, helping to reduce hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized thinking. It can also help control severe agitation, tics associated with Tourette syndrome, and behavioral problems. In some cases, it is used short-term to manage severe nausea or agitation in hospital settings.
how_it_works: Your brain uses chemical messengers to send signals, and one of the main ones is called dopamine. In conditions like schizophrenia, dopamine activity can become overactive, leading to symptoms like hearing voices or confused thinking. Haloperidol works by blocking certain dopamine receptors in the brain, which helps calm those overactive signals and reduce symptoms.
common_side_effects: Feeling drowsy or sleepy, restlessness or a need to keep moving (called akathisia), muscle stiffness or spasms, dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, dizziness when standing up quickly, and weight changes. Some people notice their muscles feel tight or their movements slow down.
warnings: This medication can cause a serious movement disorder called tardive dyskinesia, which may involve uncontrolled facial or body movements and can sometimes be permanent, so report any unusual movements right away. It may also cause a rare but dangerous reaction called Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome with high fever, muscle rigidity, and confusion — seek emergency care immediately if this happens. Haloperidol can affect heart rhythm (QT prolongation), so tell your doctor about all other medications you take. It should be used with great caution in elderly patients with dementia, as it increases the risk of serious events including stroke. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication.
typical_dosing: Dosing varies widely depending on the condition being treated. For adults with schizophrenia, a typical starting dose is 0.5 to 5 mg taken 2 to 3 times daily by mouth, and your doctor will adjust based on how you respond. A long-acting injectable form (Decanoate) is given once a month by a healthcare provider for people who prefer not to take daily pills. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions.
